hiper-conexoes.d: Generalization of the residual in which each token carries \(n\) residual streams (\(H \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\)) and each sublayer has three learned operators: read (\(n \to 1\)), write (\(1 \to n\)) and mixing between streams (\(n\times n\)). With \(n = 1\) you get the classic residual back.

hc-mult.d: Expansion rate of hyper-connections: how many residual streams each token carries. It is 4 in GLM and DeepSeek (hc_dim = 4 × 4096 = 16,384) and in Qwen (4 × 2560 = 10,240).

hc-expand.d: Entry point of a wide-residual stack: the token embedding is repeated across the \(n\) streams (x.unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, hc_mult, 1)).

mhc.d: Manifold-constrained hyper-connections (DeepSeek): dynamic hyper-connections whose 4×4 mix is projected by Sinkhorn-Knopp onto the polytope of doubly stochastic matrices, which bounds the norm by 1. Used in GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

sinkhorn-knopp.d: Algorithm that turns a positive matrix into a doubly stochastic one by alternating column and row normalizations. In mHC, hc_sinkhorn_iters = 20 iterations (39 normalizations after a row-wise softmax).

matriz-duplamente-estocastica.d: Matrix with non-negative entries whose rows and columns sum to 1. It has spectral norm ≤ 1, is closed under products and preserves the mean of the vectors it mixes.

politopo-de-birkhoff.d: The set of \(n\times n\) doubly stochastic matrices. Its vertices are the \(n!\) permutation matrices (Birkhoff-von Neumann theorem). It is the “manifold” in the name mHC.

norma-espectral.d: \(\lVert A\rVert_2\): the largest factor by which \(A\) can stretch a vector (the largest singular value). For products, \(\lVert AB\rVert_2 \le \lVert A\rVert_2\,\lVert B\rVert_2\).

ganho-de-sinal.d: How much a signal is amplified as it passes through the composition of the residual mixes of all layers. With free hyper-connections it reaches ~3,000 (mHC paper); with the doubly stochastic constraint it is bounded by 1.

hc-post.d: Operation that applies mHC's write and mix, \(H' = \text{comb}^{\top} H + \text{post} \otimes y\). In vLLM it is deferred and fused into the next layer's pre, which is why hooks have to call it explicitly.

hc-contract.d: Contraction of GLM's 4 mHC streams into a 4096-wide vector by taking the mean. Used at the end of the stack and at the EAGLE-3 taps of patch_glm_eagle3.py.

hc-head.d: Final read of DeepSeek's mHC: 4 streams → 1 with \(\sigma(\cdot)+\varepsilon\) weights predicted per token (hc_head_fn [4, 16384]), without Sinkhorn, before the final norm and the lm_head.

fusao-post-pre.d: Single kernel (MHCFusedPostPreOp) that applies one sub-block's post and immediately computes the next one's pre, reading and writing the wide state once. That is why each layer returns (hidden, residual, post, comb).

gated-residual.d: Qwen3.8's wide residual: 4 branches of 2560, a read with a rank-320 elementwise gate \(\sigma(W_u\,\mathrm{SiLU}(W_d\,\mathrm{vec}(\hat R)/4))\) (which replaces the pre-norm), a write with one scalar per branch and no mixing between branches.

hyper-connection-mixer.d: Read-only GR (use_combine=False) at the end of Qwen's stack: it contracts the 4 branches into 2560 numbers and replaces the final RMSNorm before the lm_head.

gatednorm.d: RMSNorm followed by a low-rank elementwise gate: \(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(u) \odot \sigma(W_2\,\mathrm{SiLU}(W_1\,\mathrm{RMSNorm}(u)))\). According to the Qwen3.8 tech report, it reduces activation outliers and training spikes; it is the read of the Gated Residual.

gating-multiplicativo.d: Multiplying a signal, element by element, by a factor in (0, 1) computed from the data itself (usually a sigmoid). It lets the network open and close channels token by token.

captura-diferida.d: In DeepSeek's Stage-C image (lane B, historical/optional), a target layer's feature is written by the next layer, during its mhc_fused_post_pre, without breaking the fusion: 41 captures 40 and 42 captures 41; 42, the last one, stays on the default path, which costs nothing there. The exact mode uses the dspark_hc_post_mean kernel, which rereads the wide state but doesn't write the 4 streams.

altup.d: Alternating Updates (Baykal et al., 2023): widens the residual into several branches, read through a weighted sum and written one at a time. In the simplified variant of the Qwen tech report, 4 branches with round-robin writes already reduce the loss by ~0.01.

cola-hc.d: Everything that happens between two sublayers of an mHC model: the hc_post of the one that just finished and the hc_pre of the next (24 dot products over 16,384 columns, a sum of squares, Sinkhorn, the weighted read and RMSNorm). It works row by row without mixing tokens, so it can be split by rows across ranks, as the GLM·TF recipe does in prefill.
